mechanism_narrative: A higher value of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) at t-1mo, as an indicator of inflationary pressure, erodes real corporate profit margins through increased input costs and wage pressures, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in high CPIAUCSL periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0% as of t-1mo) signals an overheated labor market that fuels wage inflation, prompting aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which reduces equity valuations through higher discount rates and thus produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE < 4.0% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) from t-2mo to t-1mo signals robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth through stronger consumer spending and thus producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rise > 0.5% and RSAFS rise > 0.5% from t-2mo to t-1mo
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) from t-2mo to t-1mo signals an imminent manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate earnings expectations and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion periods with INDPRO decline are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% (as of t-1mo) indicates restrictive monetary policy, increasing the cost of capital and suppressing equity valuations through higher discount rates, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS > 5.0% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) at t-2mo, as an indicator of strong consumer demand for housing, supports construction sector growth and accelerates corporate revenue cycles, thus producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high HOUST periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) from t-2mo to t-1mo signals coordinated monetary easing and labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rise > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS decline > 0.1% from t-2mo to t-1mo
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when PAYEMS rises > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS declines > 0.1% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A level of industrial production (INDPRO) above 110.0 (as of t-1mo) indicates robust manufacturing output, accelerating corporate revenue growth through stronger industrial demand and thus producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods with INDPRO > 110.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
